question: ‘Sangita Ratnakara’ by Pandit Sarngadeva is a _______ Century treatise on Indian classical music.
solution:
The correct answer is __**13th.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The** Sangita-Ratnakara **is **Sanskrit **for **"Ocean of Music and Dance."**
 
• It is one of the most significant Indian** texts on musicology.**
 
• In the** thirteenth centur**y, **Sarngadeva **wrote it in** Sanskrit.**
 
• The author served in **King Singhana II's court **during the **Yadava dynasty**, whose seat of government was in** Devagiri, Maharashtra**.
 
• There are** seven chapters** in the text.
 
• **Svaragatadhyaya, Ragavivekadhyaya, Prakirnakadhyaya, Prabandhadhyaya, Taladhyaya, and Vadyadhyaya,** the first six chapters, cover a variety o**f musical topics and instruments.**
 
• **Nartanadhyaya's** final chapter discusses **dance.**
